youtube.title: The CIA Finally Admitted Area 51 Exists — and Explained the UFOs
youtube.description:
For decades the US government would not acknowledge Area 51. In August 2013, the National Security Archive published the CIA's declassified history "The Central Intelligence Agency and Overhead Reconnaissance: The U-2 and OXCART Programs, 1954–1974", obtained through a records request by Jeffrey Richelson. Earlier releases had redacted the base; this one named Area 51 and the facility at Groom Lake, Nevada, chosen as the test site for the U-2 spy plane. Kelly Johnson called it "the Paradise Ranch" to make the remote site sound more attractive to workers. The history also says high-altitude U-2 testing led to "a tremendous increase in reports of unidentified flying objects," and that U-2 and later OXCART flights "accounted for more than one-half of all UFO reports during the late 1950s and most of the 1960s."

📂 Case File #032: Area 51

Sources: CIA, "The Central Intelligence Agency and Overhead Reconnaissance: The U-2 and OXCART Programs, 1954–1974" (declassified 2013), via the National Security Archive, Electronic Briefing Book No. 434; CBC News and Christian Science Monitor coverage (August 2013).
